title: History of Psychology - Module 1
description: This is the general course introduction for the PsyC85: History of Psychology being offered at UTSC.  I go over the syllabus and generally discuss the course and its structure.

title: Module 2A - Jacob's Ladder or Ixiom's Wheel
description: This video is the lecture to go with the first part of Chapter 1 in our Summer 2020 History of Psychology course at the University of Toronto Scarborough (PsyC85).  We begin by thinking about history texts in general, and histories of science specifically ... what are some things we should be aware

title: Module 2B - Social Construction
description: Associated with the end of Chapter 1 from my PsyC85 History of Psychology class (at UTSC).  In this video I make the argument that scientists are humans ... no really!

title: Module 2C - The Looming Ancients
description: This video and the next are associated with Chapter 2 of our History of Psychology class (Summer 2020 class of PsyC85 at UTSC).  This one focuses on the ancients who held that the ultimate expression of understanding was the ability to express it using math and numbers.

title: Module 2D - Aristotle, Averros & Aquinus
description: This is the last video associated with Chapter 2 of our text for the History of Psychology course at UTSC.  As the title implies, this one focuses on the impact of Aristotle, Averros and Aquinus

title: Module 3A - Descartes & Newton
description: The first lecture for Module 3 of our PsyC85 History of Psychology course.  This one corresponds to the first part of Chapter 3

title: Module 3B - British Empiricists Plus
description: Continuing along through Chapter 3, this time focusing mostly on the influence of the British Empiricists

title: Module 3C - Darwin
description: The last part of Chapter 3 ... this video is featured on Darwin and his impact on psychology

title: Module 3D - Herbart & Fechner
description: Two of the critical figures showing ways to do psychology that included mathematic descriptions of data.   This is Chapter 4 in our text.

title: Module 3E - Helmhotlz, Colour & Phrenology
description: The second video associate with Chapter 4 in our course text.  As advertised, this one focuses on Helmhotlz and his theory of colour sensation (as developed further by others) ... then ends with a discussion of phrenology.

title: Module 3C - Darwin and stuff
description: This covers the rest of Chapter 3 ... which is mostly Darwin :)

title: Module 3F - Galton & Spencer
description: The last lecture for Chapter 4, this one dealing with Galton and Spencer, and some of the ways they've considered evolution theory within a psychological context ... sometimes VERY controversially!

title: Office Hours - PsyA01 and PsyC85, Summer 2020
description: This is really a plea to you all to consider using our online office hours as a context for practicing what I call digital attentive interactions (or something like that!) ... a skill that I think will be very relevant in your future.

title: Module 4A _ Willhelm Wundt, the Father of Psychology
description: Chapter 5 begins here!  This video focuses the varied contributions of Willhelm Wundt, and why we think of him as the father of psychology.

title: Module 4B - Ebbinghaus & Calkins
description: Continuing on with Chapter 5, this lecture highlights the contributions of Hermann Von Ebbinghaus and Mary Whiton Calkins

title: Module 4C - Brentano and the Würzburg School
description: This video covers the last part of Chapter 5, kind of coming full circle on some of Wundt's ideas by highlighting how the Würzburg school took them a different direction.

title: Module 4D - King James
description: Of course I mean the King James of Psychology, not that annoying basketball player that beat out the Raptors.  We're talking William James in both this and the next video, both covering Chapter 6 of our course.

title: Module 4E - King James II
description: This covers the end of Chapter 6, still focused squarely on William James

title: peerScholar #1 - Assignment Info for PsyC85
description: In this video I describe our first peerScholar activity of the term, highlighting expectations and due dates as I do

title: Embedding Video in peerScholar
description: Short video for my PsyC85 class to show them how to embed videos in peerScholar

title: Module 5A - Sigmund Freud
description: This is the beginning of Chapter 7 for our History of Psychology Class at UTSC (PsyC85).  This lecture focuses on Sigmund Freud

title: Module 5B - Anna Freud, Alfred Adler & Karen Horney
description: Continuing on through Chapter 7, this video focuses on some of the twists others have added to Freud's general theory, including those by his daughter Anna.  It is the second of three videos for this chapter.

title: Module 5C - Carl Jung
description: This one takes us to the end of Chapter 7 and focuses exclusively on Carl Jung.

title: Module 6A - Functionalism as a reaction to structuralism
description: This video begins Chapter 8.  You will learn a lot about Titchener and his clear definition of what he thought psychology was about.  In so doing he defined a structuralist perspective on what should and should not count as psychology.  Many disagreed with his strict definition and countered with a

title: Module 6B - Intelligence
description: Lecture 2 on Chapter 8, this one focuses on early attempts to define and quantify intelligence.  It features such people as Cattell, Binet and Lewis Terman

title: Module 6C - Takin Care of Business
description: The 3rd video (of 4) for Chapter 8, this one focuses on those who brought psychology into the world of business ... including Taylor and Mayo. This is the birth of what we now call Industrial Psychology or Industrial Organization.

title: Module 6D - Comparative Psychology
description: The last lecture for Chapter 8, this one focuses on the rise of comparative psychology and the influence of people like Romanes, Morgan and - of course - Edward Thorndike.  It is the period just before Behaviourism takes over psychology in America, and one can see the foundation being laid in the wo

title: Module 6E - The Russians
description: We're now beginning Chapter 9 of our textbook.  This lecture will focus on Pavlov and Bechterev and how the set the stage for behaviourism in the United States

title: Module 6F - Watson and Lashley
description: John B Watson, Father of Behaviourism, now makes his appearance!  Inspired by the work of Pavlov, he redefined the study of psychology, at least "As the Behaviourist Views It"

title: Module 6G - Skinner
description: We're now at the end of Chapter 9 and will focus here on the work of B. F. Skinner, the radical behaviourist!

title: Module 6G - Skinner
description: This is the end of the Behaviourism chapter wherein we encounter the radical behaviourist himself, one B. F. Skinner

title: Module 7A - Wertheimer and Gestalt Psychology
description: We're starting Chapter 10 here, and suddenly a reductionist view of mental processing will be under attack!  First from the Gestalt Psychologists but soon their way of thinking will give rise to Social Psychology.  This video will focus on the first Gestalt Psychologist, Max Wetheimer

title: Module 7B - Köhlers, Koffka and Lewin
description: This is the middle part of Chapter 10, where we move from class Gestalt Psychology through to some extensions of the basic "whole system" or "holistic processing" idea that will - in our next lecture - bring us to Social Psychology proper.

title: Module 7C - Social Psychology is Born
description: This video covers the last part of Chapter 10 and focuses squarely on the first experiments in the field of social psychology, experiments that are now widely known and covered in virtually every Introduction to Psychology textbook.

title: Module 7D - Research Methods: Experimental
description: Now we're into the beginning of Chapter 11.  In this chapter we'll discuss how research methods became more formalized in the 1920 - 193X era thanks largely to the work of the Vienna Circle.  This lecture will focus on the formalization of experimental methods

title: Module 7E - Research Methods: Correlational
description: This covers the end of Chapter 11, focusing on correlation and factor analysis, its creation, and some of the ways it has been used,

title: Module 8A - Hilgard, Guthrie, Hull and Tolman
description: Welcome to Chapter 12, a world after behaviourism but before the Cognitive Revolution.  This is a time of learning theorists, researchers who began thinking about "intervening variables" ... things related to learning the occurred between the stimulus and the response.  In this lecture we meet four

title: Module 8B - Verbal Learning
description: Midway through Chapter 12 we learn about the verbal learning tradition that was a big part of informing learning theories, and also contributed many tasks and experimental traditions that continue to be commonly used in modern psychology experiments.  This video focuses on that work.

title: Module 8C - Hebb, Sperry and Bandura
description: This is the third and last video for Chapter 12 - Learning Theories.  This one actually highlights two different approaches to understanding learning, one the focuses on a brain-based perspective (Hebb & Sperry) and another that focuses on the importance of social influences on learning (Bandura).

title: Second peerScholar activity
description: In this video I describe the second peerScholar activity for our PsyC85 History of Psychology course.  Simulating conversations between famous psychologists!

title: pS1 Justification of Grading Approach
description: A video for those of you who felt the grading of peerScholar #1 was "unfair" or just too tough.

title: Module 9A - Recapitulation (Hall and Baldwin)
description: This video covers the beginning of our Chapter 13, a chapter that highlights them emergence of seeing human through a developmental lens.  This video will cover two figures from the turn of the 20th Century - G. Stanley Hall and Mark Baldwin - highlighting how each favoured variants of a "recapitula

title: Module 9B - Piaget & Vygotsky
description: The second of three lectures from Chapter 13, this one focuses on two of the giants of development psychology and educational psychology; Jean Piaget and Lev Vygotsky.

title: Module 9C - Erikson & E. Gibson
description: This is the last lecture related to Chapter 13 - Developmental Psychology.  In this one we discuss the work of Erik Erikson and Eleanor Gibson

title: Module 10A - Existential Philosophy
description: If you have not encountered existential philosophy before, prepare to have your mind messed with!  This is the beginning of Chapter 14 and it sets the stage for some of the Humanistic approaches to psychology we will discuss next.

title: Module 10B - May and Maslow
description: Now that you have a sense of existential philosophy, we'll discuss how Humanistic Psychology emerged and was situated within existentialism.  We'll discuss Rollo May and Abraham Maslow and the way their ideas - Maslow's especially - came to be widely embraced by the public, but not so much by experi

title: Module 10C - Rogers, Gendlin and Kelly
description: This video covers the end of Chapter 14 and focused on the humanistic approach to therapy and well being in general.  We'll discuss the work and ideas of Rogers, Gendlin and Kelly.

title: Module 11A - Chomsky, Miller, Bruner & Bartlett
description: This begins Chapter 15, our second last chapter.  The focus of this chapter is the Cognitive Revolution, and this particular lecture will cover the contributions of Chomsky, Miller, Bruner and Bartlett, all of whom challenged the limitations of behaviourism while demonstrating that a scientific inve

title: Module 11B - Neisser, Gibson, Simon and the Role of Computers
description: This lecture covers the end of Chapter 15, and really lays out the early days of Cognitive Psychology.  I emphasize how important computers have been, first in providing an analogy to human information processing, but later becoming tools for computational theories of mind.

title: Module 11C - The Future of the History of Psychology
description:
Dumm de dum dum ... here we are, at the end of the course!  Chapter 16.  I don't follow the text completely here so make sure you read this chapter as well as watching this lecture.

I hope you enjoyed the course and I wish you all the best! - Steve
